defects: Hypothesis mismatch: the produced ∃! condition (∃! pair (p1,p2) with p1∈supp f, p2∈supp g, p1*p2=a0*b0) does not require the unique witnessing pair to be (a0,b0) itself, whereas gold's `UniqueMul f.coeff.support g.coeff.support a0 b0` forces any decomposition of a0*b0 via supp f × supp g to equal (a0,b0). These are materially different: one can construct a0,b0 not lying in the respective supports where a distinct pair (a1,b1)≠(a0,b0) is the unique decomposition of a0*b0, satisfying the produced hypothesis while making the produced conclusion (coeff (f*g) (a0*b0) = f.coeff a0 * g.coeff b0) false, since the true value is f.coeff a1 * g.coeff b1. Thus the produced statement is not equivalent to (and is not even a true generalization of) the gold theorem.

Produced hypothesis requires existence of a decomposition (via ∃!), while gold's UniqueMul also covers the vacuous case where a0*b0 has no decomposition at all as a product from supp f × supp g (hypothesis still holds trivially, conclusion 0=0); the produced statement excludes this case, narrowing/changing the hypothesis scope.

Unnecessary strengthening of typeclass assumptions: produced requires [Monoid M] (identity + associativity) whereas gold only assumes [Mul A], which is the minimal structure actually needed for the statement.
